title: Consecutive Check Numbers Per Account
description: A bank keeps a checks table logging the check number written against each account; a row with voided = 1 is a cancelled check that must be ignored and that also breaks any run of consecutive check numbers. For every maximal run of consecutive check numbers on an account, return account_id, start_check_no, end_check_no (both inclusive) and num_checks (how many checks are in the run). Accounts whose checks are all voided must not appear at all. Return the rows ordered by account_id ascending, then start_check_no ascending.
solutionQuery: WITH valid AS (SELECT account_id, check_no FROM checks WHERE voided = 0), grouped AS (SELECT account_id, check_no, check_no - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY check_no) AS island_key FROM valid) SELECT account_id, MIN(check_no) AS start_check_no, MAX(check_no) AS end_check_no, COUNT(*) AS num_checks FROM grouped GROUP BY account_id, island_key ORDER BY account_id ASC, start_check_no ASC
explanation: First filter out voided rows, because a cancelled check must not be counted and it splits a run. Then the classic gaps-and-islands trick: subtract ROW_NUMBER() (partitioned per account, ordered by check_no) from check_no, which is constant for every consecutive sequence and changes whenever a gap appears, producing island_key. Grouping by account_id and island_key yields MIN/MAX/COUNT for each run, and accounts whose checks were all voided disappear because they never enter the CTE.
